phase1.evidence: Round2 independent review: analysis/round2/review.md and independent-review.json; primary analysis/redirect/r1-assets-stage-damage/ui-paint-decode-corrected.json; ui-paint-listing.txt; coherent complete control/data/hardware contract; adjacent data origins independently bounded

regions.summary: A supplies the fill/style mode and Y chooses a window layout. Draw vertical sides at stride eight and matching top/bottom spans in RAM $0500. Negative mode retains side tiles; zero clears the horizontal spans. Layout tables supply offsets, heights, widths and tile sequences. This builds a CPU buffer; it does not directly write VRAM.

regions.summary: A is an encoded metatile: its high two bits select palette, low six bits select a four-tile group. Two ASL/ROL pairs preserve the palette bits in scratch low bits and tile base in draw_tile_base. Convert the staged nametable address to its attribute address and derive quadrant index from address bits 1 and 6. Initial upper scratch bits are irrelevant because the palette consumer masks with three. Read the addressed attribute with the PPU dummy read preserved. AttributeInsertMasks selects the quadrant; preserve all other bits, insert the palette pattern from AttributePatternValues, then rewrite the same attribute address. PPU latch and sequential buffered-read behavior are part of this direct VRAM operation. Write the metatile base and base OR two to the top row. Add $20 to the inherited address with carry for the bottom row, and write base OR one and base OR three. Return normally; PPU increment mode must already be horizontal. This forms the four-tile group without altering unrelated attribute quadrants.
